description:
Changes:
* Removed old animation blend query
* Removed duplicate work in fbx_complex_transform query
* Refactored fbx_complex_transform

Test: 400 instances of single animated character with fbx_complex_transforms:

FPS: 20 -> 40
Overall improvement: 50~ ms / frame -> 24~ ms / frame
animation_systems 15.5 ms -> 7.5 ms
TransformSystem::run 29 ms -> > 12.5 ms

Before:
[Before](https://github.com/AmbientRun/Ambient/assets/71590722/dcd540d2-d02f-4f6c-a589-d42285a6dfe1)

After:
[After](https://github.com/AmbientRun/Ambient/assets/71590722/250c3d44-f873-4d78-8ebe-f0439b6a0d4b)

fbx_complex_transform is now about 3ms of the work, the rest is transform propagation. I would probably remove completely it unless someone has good reason for it to stay. 

Perf is not horrible but the animation sampling as a lot of room for improvement. The transform system I'm not so sure about but obviously all of this could be parallelized.

comments.body: I'm not sure that they will always have _all_ of these components, which was why it was implemented as it was.
Oh I see, you're always setting them now. Yeah I guess that's fine
What's the relationship between AnimationAction and the AnimationStack?

Yeah, I did an unsound optional variant that got a modest ~25% increase in performance. I think in the case of transforms it should be worth to spend a little bit more on memory to utilize the hardware better.

AnimationStack samples AnimtionActions by index, the idea is that you could preload the animations and then blend them as you need every frame. I'm hoping this will also make it straightforward to extend the blending with procedural poses that produces a consistent result if nothing else.

I'm not sure this is the end game of the animation system but what I'm trying to be considerate about at this moment is the amount of data that needs to be transferred from guest every frame. As that's what I'm hearing is problematic with WASM in the browser. It may be that guest won't even interact with this system at this "low level" and then it might not even matter.

Hm isn't AnimationActions and AnimationStack doing the same thing then? AnimationActions are a list of animations with parameters of how they should be blended together; AnimationStack seems to be doing the same thing? Or is there a reason why both are needed? (It's quite a while since I looked at this though)

For pre-loading we should just be able to `AnimationClipRef::XX {].peek()` to preload that animation.

They are, the difference being one is doing stack operations with option doing a masked blend. AnimationStack makes it straightforward to produce the right order of operations. 

I tried to use AnimationActions todo the same things a few weeks ago but it felt confusing to get the right blend when transitioning.

As for the preloading, I'm thinking more like a AnimationSet rather than individual clips.
